note: This unit ties together every construction from Units 1–7 — extended attributes, stacked nominal attributes, embedded clauses, concession, focus — into an explicit toolkit for reading and building the genuinely long sentences C1 texts use.

examples.de: C1-Texte verbinden erweiterte Attribute, Nominalstil und eingebettete Nebensätze zu langen, vielschichtigen Sätzen.
examples.en: C1 texts combine extended attributes, nominal style, and embedded subordinate clauses into long, multi-layered sentences.

note: The finite verb in position 2, its infinitives/participles/separable prefixes at the very end — the skeleton every German sentence obeys, however many layers get packed inside it.

examples.de: Er hat das Projekt trotz aller Widerstände erfolgreich abgeschlossen.
examples.en: He successfully completed the project despite all the resistance.

english: a nested sentence (multiply embedded subordinate clauses)
note: A sentence with subordinate clauses nested inside other subordinate clauses — each with its own verb-final position, several layers deep.

examples.de: Er sagte, dass er glaube, dass die Lösung, die sie vorgeschlagen hatten, funktionieren werde.
examples.en: He said he believed the solution they had proposed would work.

english: a subordinate clause inside a subordinate clause
note: Concretely: a relative clause or dass-clause embedded inside another subordinate clause — very common when a reported claim itself contains a description.

examples.de: Sie erklärte, dass das Ergebnis, das die Forscher veröffentlicht hatten, große Aufmerksamkeit erregte.
examples.en: She explained that the result, which the researchers had published, attracted great attention.

english: verbs piling up at multiple clause ends
note: When clauses nest, several finite and non-finite verbs accumulate near each other at clause boundaries — the key reading skill is working out which verb belongs to which clause.

examples.de: Sie erklärte, dass sie den Vertrag, den sie unterschrieben hatte, bereute.
examples.en: She explained that she regretted the contract she had signed.

note: Certain elements — a comparison, a prepositional phrase, an infinitive clause — can be placed after the normal final-verb position instead of being crammed into the Mittelfeld, for clarity or weight.

examples.de: Er ist schneller gelaufen, als wir erwartet hatten.
examples.en: He ran faster than we had expected.

note: The most common Nachfeld case: an als/wie comparison trails after the sentence's final verb rather than sitting awkwardly before it.

examples.de: Das Projekt war komplizierter, als alle gedacht hatten.
examples.en: The project was more complicated than everyone had thought.

english: an infinitive clause in the post-field
note: An um…zu, ohne…zu, or anstatt…zu clause placed after the final verb, rather than packed into the middle field — keeps the core sentence readable.

examples.de: Er verließ den Raum, ohne ein Wort zu sagen.
examples.en: He left the room without saying a word.

note: Generalises B1's relative-clause Einschub: any aside — a comment, a qualification, a reported detail — can interrupt a sentence mid-flow, marked by commas, dashes, or brackets.

examples.de: Das Projekt – so hieß es zumindest offiziell – sei termingerecht abgeschlossen worden.
examples.en: The project – or so it was officially said, at least – had allegedly been completed on schedule.

note: A noun phrase placed right next to another to rename or specify it, set off by commas — a compact alternative to a whole relative clause.

examples.de: Angela Merkel, ehemalige Bundeskanzlerin, hielt die Eröffnungsrede.
examples.en: Angela Merkel, former chancellor, gave the opening speech.

english: reading strategy: finding the core sentence
note: Strip away every attribute, embedded clause, and parenthetical aside to find the bare subject–verb–object core first, then add the layers back in one at a time.

examples.de: Kernsatz: "Die Erhöhung tritt in Kraft." — alles andere sind Attribute und Nebensätze, die sich Schritt für Schritt ergänzen lassen.
examples.en: Core sentence: "The increase takes effect." — everything else is attributes and subordinate clauses that can be added back step by step.

note: The reverse move for writing: start from a simple core sentence, then deliberately add one layer at a time — an attribute, an embedded clause, a Nachfeld element — without losing control of it.

examples.de: Schritt 1: Die Erhöhung tritt in Kraft. Schritt 2: Die vom Ministerium beschlossene Erhöhung tritt im Januar in Kraft.
examples.en: Step 1: The increase takes effect. Step 2: The increase decided by the ministry takes effect in January.

english: the colon for structuring a sentence
note: A colon introduces a list, an explanation, or a conclusion within a longer sentence — a punctuation-level tool for managing density without starting a new sentence.

examples.de: Die Untersuchung kommt zu einem eindeutigen Ergebnis: Die Maßnahme zeigt keine Wirkung.
examples.en: The investigation reaches a clear conclusion: the measure has no effect.

note: Links two closely related independent clauses without a full stop or a coordinating conjunction — common in the dense, connector-heavy style from Unit 4.

examples.de: Die Nachfrage sinkt; die Preise bleiben dennoch stabil.
examples.en: Demand is falling; prices nevertheless remain stable.

note: The overall organisation of a text into its parts — die Gliederung eines Aufsatzes.

examples.de: Die Gliederung des Aufsatzes folgt einem klaren Schema.
examples.en: The essay's structure follows a clear pattern.

note: A defined part of a longer text — der erste/letzte Abschnitt.

examples.de: Der erste Abschnitt fasst die Ausgangslage zusammen.
examples.en: The first section summarises the starting situation.

note: The general word for how something is organised — die Struktur eines Satzes/Textes.

examples.de: Die Struktur des Satzes wirkt auf den ersten Blick verwirrend.
examples.en: The structure of the sentence seems confusing at first glance.

note: Close to Struktur, but leans toward how something was built up piece by piece — der Aufbau eines Textes. No natural plural in this sense.

examples.de: Der Aufbau des Textes folgt der klassischen Dreiteilung.
examples.en: The composition of the text follows the classic three-part structure.

note: Describes a sentence or structure with many layers embedded inside each other — from the same root as Schachtelsatz.

examples.de: Der Satz ist stark verschachtelt und schwer zu lesen.
examples.en: The sentence is heavily nested and hard to read.

note: How easy a text is to take in at a glance — der Übersichtlichkeit halber (for the sake of clarity). No natural plural.

examples.de: Der Übersichtlichkeit halber wurde der Satz in zwei Sätze geteilt.
examples.en: For the sake of clarity, the sentence was split into two.

note: Describes a text or structure that's hard to take in at a glance — the opposite of übersichtlich.

examples.de: Der Absatz wirkt unübersichtlich.
examples.en: The paragraph seems cluttered.

note: Describes a text that communicates clearly despite its content or length — trotz seiner Länge gut verständlich.

examples.de: Der Text ist trotz seiner Länge gut verständlich.
examples.en: The text is easy to understand despite its length.

note: The noun matching verständlich — how easily a text can be understood. No natural plural.

examples.de: Die Verständlichkeit leidet unter den vielen Schachtelsätzen.
examples.en: The comprehensibility suffers from the many nested sentences.

note: A specific location within a text being referred to — diese Textstelle, an dieser Textstelle.

examples.de: Diese Textstelle ist besonders schwer zu entschlüsseln.
examples.en: This passage is particularly hard to decipher.

note: To divide a text or argument into clearly separated parts — einen Text in Abschnitte gliedern.

examples.de: Der Autor gliedert seinen Text in drei Abschnitte.
examples.en: The author structures his text into three sections.

note: To cut a text down and make it more concise without losing its content — einen Absatz straffen.

examples.de: Der zweite Absatz sollte gestrafft werden.
examples.en: The second paragraph should be tightened up.

note: The general word for something made of many interrelated parts — ein komplexer Sachverhalt.

examples.de: Der Sachverhalt ist ausgesprochen komplex.
examples.en: The matter is exceptionally complex.

note: A block of text forming one unit of a longer piece of writing — einen neuen Absatz beginnen. (Absatz also means a shoe heel or business turnover in other contexts; the paragraph sense is clear from context.)

examples.de: Jeder neue Gedanke beginnt einen neuen Absatz.
examples.en: Every new idea begins a new paragraph.
